tier_rationale: Crafter is a synchronous local Gym environment: the simulation advances one tick only when the adaptor calls step(action). Hunger, thirst, energy, day/night, plants and mobs advance between actions, but waiting for Astra while no step is issued does not consume game time. Decisions can therefore take seconds to a minute without an in-game deadline; the practical limit is the harness wall-clock budget.

interface.why: The upstream Python environment is the benchmark's deterministic simulator, works offline and headless, exposes exact discrete actions plus inventory and achievement mappings, and avoids GUI capture or account/network dependencies. A version-checked private-world serializer can provide the requested semantic local map.
software: pygame and the Gym/Gymnasium dependency required by the pinned Crafter release

env.description: Set to dummy on headless Linux if Pygame initializes a display

setup_steps: Install Crafter and pinned dependencies into /home/hemlix/GamingMaster-mh-tier1/runs/venvs/crafter using offline wheels.
Smoke-test Env.reset(seed), Env.step, action_space and observation_space; record the installed version and action-name mapping.
Implement a version-checked serializer for the public inventory/achievements and nearby world/player state (or a local RGB tile decoder fallback).
Implement reset(seed), synchronous step(action), old/new Gym tuple compatibility, and close in finally.
Run headless with SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy and test several held-out integer seeds.
interface.observation: Public observations provide RGB image plus inventory and achievements mappings (and reward/discount, with exact keys release-dependent). The adaptor should add JSON text containing a radius tile/entity grid, player coordinates/facing/vitals, inventory, achievements and recent transition; use env private world/player objects when present and retain image optionally.
interface.actions: Submit one discrete integer per step: noop, four directional moves, do/interact, sleep, and place stone/table/furnace/plant. Resolve IDs from env.action_space/package names at startup and advance only through Env.step(action).

scoring: Report achievements unlocked per episode and the benchmark Crafter score: aggregate achievement success rates over held-out seeds (the paper defines the aggregate as a geometric mean). Do not use shaped reward as the primary score; it does not represent the named objectives.
scenarios: Call reset(seed) with many fresh integer seeds for evaluation, preserving the standard world size and episode length. Use fixed seeds only for debugging. Held-out seeds should vary procedural terrain, resource locations, water/food proximity and enemy encounters; do not memorize routes.
strategy_summary: Strong play follows the dependency chain wood -> table/wood tools -> stone -> furnace/coal -> iron -> diamond, while drinking, eating and planting before those vitals become critical. Maintain a semantic local map, face targets before do, batch only short safe action sequences, and replan after every meaningful step because mobs, day/night and resources change. Crafting legality, inventory, recipes, coordinates and achievement accounting belong in code; Astra chooses objectives and routes; Jev answers fast urgency, target, combat and legal-action questions. Kite enemies and retreat when health or supplies are low rather than pursuing a marginal achievement.
risks: The package may be unavailable in the offline wheel cache or its Gym/Pygame dependency versions may conflict with Python 3.12.
The semantic map is not a stable public field; private world/player attributes are release-sensitive, so pin and smoke-test, with RGB decoding as fallback.
Long no-op/action sequences consume game ticks and can cause starvation, thirst, night combat or death.
Achievement names and observation tuple conventions vary across Crafter releases; discover them at runtime.
No external server, account or anti-cheat bypass is involved; screen injection is brittle and unnecessary.
